## Main Point

The [Creator Performance Report](../portfolio/automated_reporting/00_creator-performance-report-sample.qmd) is a high-level snapshot of creator performance across a selected reporting window. It is designed to help readers understand scale, consistency, audience behavior, monetization patterns, and content strategy signals without treating the report as a causal model or prediction system.

:::{.callout-note .note-context title="View the report"}
This companion note is meant to be read alongside the [Creator Performance Report sample](../portfolio/automated_reporting/00_creator-performance-report-sample.qmd). For chart-by-chart interpretation help, see [How to Read Creator Report Charts](07_reading_creator_report_charts.qmd).
:::

## What the Report Does

The report summarizes what happened during a selected period of time. That window might be the last 7, 30, or 90 days, or it might cover the full lifetime of available data. The reporting window matters because recent strategy, audience behavior, and posting frequency may differ from older content.

At a high level, the report brings together views, on-stream donation revenue, video counts, average and median performance, engagement distributions, audience composition, timing patterns, collaborations, topics, and classified title tags. These sections are meant to help creators and teams ask better questions about what is working and where to look more closely.

:::{.callout-note .note-scope title="Descriptive, not causal"}
The report describes historical patterns. It does not prove that a specific topic, tag, timing choice, collaboration, or content format caused higher performance.
:::

## How to Use It

Start with the overall snapshot before jumping into detailed sections. Totals show overall contribution, while averages and medians help compare per-video performance. A content type, topic, or tag can look strong because it appears often, because it performs well each time, or because one unusually successful video is pulling the result upward.

When reading any table or chart, check the video count behind the metric. Patterns based on many videos are usually more reliable than patterns based on one or two uploads. Use the report as a way to identify areas worth reviewing, not as a final verdict on what the creator should do next.

## Practical Takeaway

Use the Creator Performance Report as a structured starting point. It helps identify what deserves attention: formats with strong reach, topics with meaningful revenue, tags that repeat across successful videos, audience segments that are changing, or timing patterns that may be worth testing. The strongest decisions come from reading these patterns together rather than relying on any single chart.
